findings.title: Anchor allowance check is order-sensitive and removes the wrong occurrence
findings.body: In `santizeAnchors` the `Matcher` is built over the original `value`, but inside the loop `value` is reassigned to a shorter string via `value.replaceFirst(...)`. `replaceFirst` removes the first occurrence of the English anchor text from the current string, not the occurrence the matcher is inspecting, and because positions are taken from the old string, matching is only correct when the translation contains the anchors in exactly the same order and count as the English source. A legitimate translation that keeps both anchors but reorders them is reported as "Didn't find anchor tag" (false positive, fails the build); conversely, if English has more anchors than the translation the extra `matcher.find()` never runs and a translation that dropped a required link is not reported (false negative). This undermines the verifier's purpose. Compare the full set of anchor tags (e.g. collect and compare multisets) and strip them based on actual match positions.

findings.title: Account console message changed from i18next {{n}} to Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat
findings.body: This file is the account console's i18next catalog and everywhere else uses `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, `{{2}}` (e.g. `error-invalid-length-too-short` on line 27). The change rewrites `error-invalid-multivalued-size` to Java MessageFormat placeholders `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` plus a ChoiceFormat pattern `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`. The React account console only interpolates `{{...}}` and has no ChoiceFormat support, so if this message is displayed the user will see literal `{0}`, `{2,choice,...}` text instead of the attribute name and limits. Keep the `{{n}}` form in this catalog.

findings.title: Admin console message changed from i18next {{n}} to Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat
findings.body: The admin console catalog uses i18next `{{n}}` placeholders throughout, but this change rewrites `error-invalid-multivalued-size` to Java `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` and adds the Java-only ChoiceFormat `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`. The React admin console cannot interpret `{n}` or ChoiceFormat, so the message will render the raw placeholder/choice text for users if this key is used. This should stay in the `{{n}}` form; Java ChoiceFormat belongs only in the server-side `messages_en.properties`.

findings.title: Lithuanian account messages now contain Italian text
findings.body: The new value `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, not Lithuanian. The previous value was Lithuanian (`Įdiekite ...`), so this is a language regression that will show Italian instructions to Lithuanian users. Replace it with a Lithuanian translation (e.g. `Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo telefone:`).

findings.title: Lithuanian login messages now contain Italian text
findings.body: `loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, but this is the Lithuanian (`messages_lt.properties`) bundle and the previous value was Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see Italian instructions. Replace with a proper Lithuanian string.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese bundle got Traditional Chinese text
findings.body: The rest of this file is Simplified Chinese (`打开应用`, `应用`, `验证码`), but the new `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional characters (`手機`, `應用程式`). The locale is `zh_CN`, so this should be Simplified (`在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`); the current text is a localization regression.

findings.title: Missing English counterpart aborts build with an uncaught RuntimeException
findings.body: `verify()` only catches `IOException` and converts it to `MojoExecutionException`, but `verifySafeHtml()` throws a bare `RuntimeException` when it cannot open the derived English file (`throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e)`). If the derived path does not exist (e.g. a locale whose `_en.properties` counterpart is absent or whose name is not rewritten correctly by the `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` heuristic), the Maven build dies with a stack trace instead of a clean, aggregatable verification message. Throw `MojoExecutionException` (or surface a proper error message) so the plugin reports the problem consistently.

findings.title: Tests only cover failures; no test proves allowed HTML and matching anchors are accepted
findings.body:
All four tests assert that something is flagged (`Duplicate keys`, `Illegal HTML`, `Didn't find anchor tag`). There is no test that exercises the positive path: that a translation containing allowed HTML (`

`, ``, `
`) for an English key that has HTML is accepted, or that a translation whose ``/`` tags match the English source is accepted. Since the PR relies on `POLICY_SOME_HTML` and `santizeAnchors` to avoid false positives (and touched many translation files to satisfy the new check), the anchor-matching bug (order/count handling) and any policy regression would go unnoticed. Add fixtures where verification returns no messages for valid HTML/anchors.
